nodes.label: ADR-001: Event-Driven Core
nodes.context: Synchronous service-to-service calls were creating tight coupling and cascading failures between payments, accounts and fraud.
nodes.decision: Introduce an Apache Kafka event bus and move all cross-domain communication to asynchronous domain events.
nodes.consequences: Looser coupling and independent scaling, at the cost of eventual consistency and the need for idempotent consumers.
nodes.alternatives: Synchronous gRPC mesh; shared database integration.

nodes.label: ADR-002: Immutable Ledger on PostgreSQL
nodes.context: Financial transactions must be auditable and tamper-evident for regulators.
nodes.decision: Store transactions in an append-only PostgreSQL ledger with Patroni replication; never update or delete rows.
nodes.consequences: Strong auditability and point-in-time reconstruction; table growth requires partitioning and archival.

nodes.label: ADR-003: Stateless JWT Auth
nodes.context: Session affinity made horizontal scaling of the API tier difficult.
nodes.decision: Use short-lived signed JWT access tokens issued by Keycloak; validate at the gateway with no server-side session store.
nodes.consequences: Stateless, horizontally scalable auth; token revocation needs a short TTL plus a denylist.
nodes.alternatives: Server-side sessions in Redis; opaque tokens with introspection.

nodes.label: ADR-000: Modular Monolith
nodes.context: The initial MVP needed to ship quickly with a small team.
nodes.decision: Build the platform as a single modular monolith deployed as one unit.
nodes.consequences: Fast early delivery, but scaling and team autonomy became bottlenecks as the platform grew.

nodes.label: PSD2 & AMLD6 obligations
nodes.description:
Summary of the regulatory obligations attached to our EU payment-institution licence:

- PSD2: every payment initiated from a digital channel needs strong customer authentication, and customers must see all charges and the exchange rate before they confirm.
- AMLD6: no account may be used before customer due diligence (identity, sanctions, PEP and AML screening) is complete.
- Record keeping: decisions on suspicious payments must be reconstructable for at least five years, including who decided and why.

nodes.label: Retail payments brief
nodes.description:
Our customers move money from the mobile app and the web, and they need to trust what they see.

Support tells us people send a payment again when they are not sure the first one went through; duplicates are the top reason for calls. Balances in the app sometimes disagree with statements for a few minutes, and that worries people. Last quarter we refunded €1.2M of authorised push-payment fraud, and most of it could have been stopped if someone had looked at the payment before it left.

We want customers to always know where a payment is, to see the same balance everywhere, and suspicious payments to be caught before settlement.
nodes.source: Head of Digital Payments — product kick-off

nodes.label: Corporate treasurer feedback
nodes.description:
Notes from the quarterly call with the treasurer of one of our larger corporate clients:

- Payroll goes in as one bulk file of about 4,000 lines. Last month one bad IBAN stopped the file halfway and half the staff were paid a day late. They want to hear about all problems before anything is sent.
- Their auditors require a second signatory on every batch; today they enforce it by e-mail.
- They would like to see afterwards who approved what.
nodes.source: Relationship manager — quarterly call with a corporate client

nodes.label: PSD2-compliant payments
nodes.action: comply with PSD2 for every payment initiated through a digital channel
nodes.rationale: Operating licence condition in the EU; the child requirements break it down into testable behaviour.

nodes.label: Strong customer authentication
nodes.trigger: a customer submits a payment above €30
nodes.action: require strong customer authentication with two independent factors before the payment is released
nodes.rationale: PSD2 RTS on SCA. Approving in the bound mobile app covers possession + inherence.

nodes.label: FX & fee transparency
nodes.feature: a payment is cross-border or in a foreign currency
nodes.action: show the exchange rate, all fees and the amount the recipient receives before the customer confirms
nodes.rationale: PSD2 / Cross-Border Payments Regulation — no hidden mark-ups.

nodes.label: Instant payment confirmation
nodes.trigger: a payment is accepted for execution
nodes.action: show a confirmation with the payment reference and expected settlement date within 2 seconds
nodes.rationale: Customers retry payments they are unsure about; duplicate payments are the #1 support topic.

nodes.label: Hold high-risk payments
nodes.unwanted_condition: the fraud score of a payment exceeds the risk threshold
nodes.action: hold the payment, tell the customer it is under review and open a fraud case for an operator
nodes.rationale: Authorised push-payment fraud is refundable to the customer — stopping it before settlement is far cheaper.

nodes.label: Balances from the ledger
nodes.action: derive every displayed balance and statement from the immutable transaction ledger
nodes.rationale: One source of truth: what the customer sees is what the auditor sees.

nodes.label: Validate bulk files up front
nodes.trigger: a corporate client uploads a bulk payment file
nodes.action: validate every line (IBAN checksum, amount, duplicate reference) and report all errors before any payment in the batch is released
nodes.rationale: Partially executed payroll batches are expensive to unwind.

nodes.label: Four-eyes approval
nodes.precondition: a bulk batch totals more than €100,000
nodes.action: require approval by a second authorised signatory before the batch is submitted
nodes.rationale: Corporate mandate rules; also an internal-fraud control.

nodes.label: Auditable case decisions
nodes.action: record every operator decision on a fraud case, with reason and timestamp, in an append-only audit trail
nodes.rationale: Regulators ask why a payment was released; the answer has to be reconstructable years later.

nodes.label: KYC before activation
nodes.action: verify identity and screen against sanctions and AML lists before any account is activated
nodes.rationale: AMLD6 — no account may be used before due diligence is complete.

adr-evt.label: ADR-001: Event-Driven Core
adr-evt.context: Synchronous service-to-service calls were creating tight coupling and cascading failures between payments, accounts and fraud.
adr-evt.decision: Introduce an Apache Kafka event bus and move all cross-domain communication to asynchronous domain events.
adr-evt.consequences: Looser coupling and independent scaling, at the cost of eventual consistency and the need for idempotent consumers.
adr-evt.alternatives: Synchronous gRPC mesh; shared database integration.

adr-ledger.label: ADR-002: Immutable Ledger on PostgreSQL
adr-ledger.context: Financial transactions must be auditable and tamper-evident for regulators.
adr-ledger.decision: Store transactions in an append-only PostgreSQL ledger with Patroni replication; never update or delete rows.
adr-ledger.consequences: Strong auditability and point-in-time reconstruction; table growth requires partitioning and archival.

adr-jwt.label: ADR-003: Stateless JWT Auth
adr-jwt.context: Session affinity made horizontal scaling of the API tier difficult.
adr-jwt.decision: Use short-lived signed JWT access tokens issued by Keycloak; validate at the gateway with no server-side session store.
adr-jwt.consequences: Stateless, horizontally scalable auth; token revocation needs a short TTL plus a denylist.
adr-jwt.alternatives: Server-side sessions in Redis; opaque tokens with introspection.

adr-mono.label: ADR-000: Modular Monolith
adr-mono.context: The initial MVP needed to ship quickly with a small team.
adr-mono.decision: Build the platform as a single modular monolith deployed as one unit.
adr-mono.consequences: Fast early delivery, but scaling and team autonomy became bottlenecks as the platform grew.

req-fraud-hold.label: Hold high-risk payments
req-fraud-hold.unwanted_condition: the fraud score of a payment exceeds the risk threshold
req-fraud-hold.action: hold the payment, tell the customer it is under review and open a fraud case for an operator
req-fraud-hold.rationale: Authorised push-payment fraud is refundable to the customer — stopping it before settlement is far cheaper.

req-balance-ledger.label: Balances from the ledger
req-balance-ledger.action: derive every displayed balance and statement from the immutable transaction ledger
req-balance-ledger.rationale: One source of truth: what the customer sees is what the auditor sees.

req-bulk-validation.label: Validate bulk files up front
req-bulk-validation.trigger: a corporate client uploads a bulk payment file
req-bulk-validation.action: validate every line (IBAN checksum, amount, duplicate reference) and report all errors before any payment in the batch is released
req-bulk-validation.rationale: Partially executed payroll batches are expensive to unwind.

req-dual-approval.label: Four-eyes approval
req-dual-approval.precondition: a bulk batch totals more than €100,000
req-dual-approval.action: require approval by a second authorised signatory before the batch is submitted
req-dual-approval.rationale: Corporate mandate rules; also an internal-fraud control.

req-case-audit.label: Auditable case decisions
req-case-audit.action: record every operator decision on a fraud case, with reason and timestamp, in an append-only audit trail
req-case-audit.rationale: Regulators ask why a payment was released; the answer has to be reconstructable years later.

req-kyc.label: KYC before activation
req-kyc.action: verify identity and screen against sanctions and AML lists before any account is activated
req-kyc.rationale: AMLD6 — no account may be used before due diligence is complete.

sc-sca-approve.label: Payment approved in the mobile app
sc-sca-approve.given: Anna has a verified device bound to her account
sc-sca-approve.when: she submits a €1,000 transfer to a new payee
sc-sca-approve.then: a push challenge is sent to her mobile app
sc-sca-approve.gherkin:
And the payment is released only after she approves with Face ID
But it is cancelled if the challenge expires after 5 minutes

sc-fx-quote.label: FX quote shown before confirmation
sc-fx-quote.given: Anna holds a EUR current account
sc-fx-quote.when: she sends 1,000.00 USD-equivalent to a US IBAN
sc-fx-quote.then: the review step shows the rate 1 EUR = 1.0824 USD, a €4.50 fee and $1,082.40 received
sc-fx-quote.gherkin: And the quoted rate is locked for 30 seconds

sc-fraud-hold.label: High-risk payment is held
sc-fraud-hold.when: a payment is scored 0.91 by Fraud Detection
sc-fraud-hold.then: the payment status is "On hold" and no funds leave the account
sc-fraud-hold.gherkin:
And the customer sees the "Payment on hold" screen
And a case appears at the top of the operator queue

sc-bulk-errors.label: Invalid lines block the batch
sc-bulk-errors.given: a payroll file with 248 payments, 3 of them invalid
sc-bulk-errors.then: the validation report lists lines 17, 92 and 203 with their errors
sc-bulk-errors.gherkin: And no payment in the batch is released

sc-dual-approval.label: Same signatory cannot approve twice
sc-dual-approval.given: a €240,118 batch already approved by T. Braun
sc-dual-approval.when: T. Braun tries to approve it again

need-regulation.label: PSD2 & AMLD6 obligations
need-regulation.description:
Summary of the regulatory obligations attached to our EU payment-institution licence:

- PSD2: every payment initiated from a digital channel needs strong customer authentication, and customers must see all charges and the exchange rate before they confirm.
- AMLD6: no account may be used before customer due diligence (identity, sanctions, PEP and AML screening) is complete.
- Record keeping: decisions on suspicious payments must be reconstructable for at least five years, including who decided and why.

need-retail-brief.label: Retail payments brief
need-retail-brief.description:
Our customers move money from the mobile app and the web, and they need to trust what they see.

Support tells us people send a payment again when they are not sure the first one went through; duplicates are the top reason for calls. Balances in the app sometimes disagree with statements for a few minutes, and that worries people. Last quarter we refunded €1.2M of authorised push-payment fraud, and most of it could have been stopped if someone had looked at the payment before it left.

We want customers to always know where a payment is, to see the same balance everywhere, and suspicious payments to be caught before settlement.
need-retail-brief.source: Head of Digital Payments — product kick-off

need-corporate-feedback.label: Corporate treasurer feedback
need-corporate-feedback.description:
Notes from the quarterly call with the treasurer of one of our larger corporate clients:

- Payroll goes in as one bulk file of about 4,000 lines. Last month one bad IBAN stopped the file halfway and half the staff were paid a day late. They want to hear about all problems before anything is sent.
- Their auditors require a second signatory on every batch; today they enforce it by e-mail.
- They would like to see afterwards who approved what.
need-corporate-feedback.source: Relationship manager — quarterly call with a corporate client
